data.description:
### 1. Technical Environment

* **code_version:** 0801c20165

### 2. Incident Overview

* **Scenario Type:** User-Flagged Behavior

#### Expected Behavior

\`ticket delete\` for an isolated ticket (no incoming LINK references from any other ticket) should be O(1) on tracker size — write the STATUS(deleted) event, write the tombstone, commit. Total expected: a few seconds regardless of how many tickets exist in the tracker.

#### Actual Behavior

Every \`ticket delete\` invocation calls \`plugins/dso/scripts/ticket-delete-unlink-scan.py\`, which runs \`reduce_all_tickets()\` to enumerate every ticket in the tracker looking for active LINKs pointing at the deleted ticket. On the current local tracker:

\`\`\`
\$ python3 -c "from ticket_reducer import reduce_all_tickets; r = reduce_all_tickets('.tickets-tracker'); print(len(r))"
20072
# 8.5s
\$ time bash plugins/dso/scripts/ticket delete <isolated-test-ticket> --user-approved
real 0m21.249s
\`\`\`

Breakdown for a single delete of a freshly-created test ticket with no incoming LINKs:
* ticket create: ~4s
* ticket show: ~0.17s
* **ticket delete: ~21s**
  * Of which \`reduce_all_tickets()\` inside unlink-scan: ~8.5s (40% of delete cost)
  * Remainder: STATUS(deleted) event write, git stages, git commits, SNAPSHOT compaction

The cost is paid on every single delete — production bug closures, test cleanup, ticket archival, batch delete — regardless of whether the deleted ticket actually has any incoming LINKs. As the tracker grows, every delete gets slower.

### 3. Action History

* Local tracker accumulated 20K+ tickets across many sessions
* CI tracker has 5000+ tickets accumulated across PR runs
* Integration test \`tests/scripts/test-create-bug-detected-by-integration.sh\` exceeded 120s CI timeout when iterating over multiple channel values
* Profiling identified delete as the bottleneck (21s of the 28s 1-channel local test)

### 4. Chronological Rationalization

The unlink-scan was hardened (bugs 0071-a28d, 3932-5199 referenced in script header) to use \`reduce_all_tickets()\` for SNAPSHOT-aware scanning. The correctness improvement is real — SNAPSHOT-compacted tickets must be considered. But the perf cost is the entire reducer pass on every delete, even when no LINKs exist anywhere in the tracker.

### 5. Skills and Workflows

* Affected: any code path that deletes a ticket — \`/dso:fix-bug\` Phase G archival, \`/dso:sprint\` cleanup, \`/dso:end-session\` cleanup, test fixtures, CI workflows
* CI symptom: \`tests/scripts/test-create-bug-detected-by-integration.sh\` and \`tests/scripts/test-detected-by-audit.sh\` exceed per-test 120s budget

### 6. Logs

\`\`\`
\$ time bash plugins/dso/scripts/ticket create bug "perf test bug" --tags "CLI_user,detected_by:tests"
6ae4-78b3-764d-4a0e
real 0m4.023s

\$ time bash plugins/dso/scripts/ticket show 6ae4-78b3-764d-4a0e > /dev/null
real 0m0.167s

\$ time bash plugins/dso/scripts/ticket delete 6ae4-78b3-764d-4a0e --user-approved
Deleted ticket '6ae4-78b3-764d-4a0e'
UNBLOCKED: none
real 0m21.249s
\`\`\`

#### Suggested fix (option 1, cheap and safe)

Pre-check: grep the tracker for any file containing the deleted ticket's ID before running the full reducer pass. If no LINK or SNAPSHOT events reference the ID, no active LINKs can exist anywhere — skip the reducer call and emit zero UNLINKs.

\`\`\`bash
# Cheap pre-check
if ! grep -rl "$deleted_id" "$tracker_dir" --include="*-LINK.json" --include="*-SNAPSHOT.json" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    # No LINK or SNAPSHOT references → no active LINKs possible
    exit 0  # no unlink work needed
fi
# Else fall through to existing reducer pass
\`\`\`

Conservative semantics: false-positive-friendly. If LINK + UNLINK both reference the ID, grep matches → fall through to reducer (which correctly emits zero UNLINKs because no active LINK survives). Only the common "isolated ticket" case is short-circuited, which is the case where the current scan wastes the most work.
data.title: [ticket-delete-unlink-scan]: every delete runs full reducer -> ~9s per delete on 20K-ticket tracker
